interest: For historians, this file offers an exceptional multi-tiered perspective on post-war democratization by juxtaposing top-down Allied policy debates—including inter-Allied friction with Australia and the Soviet Union—against grassroots Japanese initiatives, student strikes, and bold domestic proposals like Chugo Watanabe's. It also provides rare empirical granular data through Dr. Leebrick's immediate post-war regional field reports and an exhaustive 1946 census of every school, student, and teacher in Akita Prefecture.
overview: This file documents the planning, implementation, and grassroots realities of post-World War II Japanese educational reform under Allied Occupation between March 1945 and March 1948. It details high-level policy formulation and directives issued by the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee (SWNCC), and the Far Eastern Commission (FEC) focusing on demilitarization, teacher screening, textbook revision, and administrative decentralization. Alongside inter-Allied diplomacy—featuring Australian policy proposals and Soviet critiques in the Allied Council for Japan—the records capture internal Japanese perspectives through Ministry of Education actions, political party platforms, student activism, educator unionization, and indigenous reform proposals such as the 6-3-3-4 system. Finally, the file provides detailed ground-level assessments of war damage, regional educational conditions, and an exhaustive 1946 statistical roster of educational institutions across Akita Prefecture.
